title: Martha, Mary and Lazarus (29 July)
hook: the Bethany family, now celebrated together on one day

segments.voice: Yesterday, James, the son of thunder, and the long road to his tomb in Spain. Your line was the way of saint james.

There's a guest in the house, and the kitchen is chaos. Bread to bake, water to fetch, a meal to get on the table. One sister is doing all of it. The other sits on the floor in the next room, listening. The busy one finally comes out, hands still floured, and says it out loud: tell her to help me. The guest is Jesus. The house is in Bethany, a village near Jerusalem, and the three who live there, two sisters and a brother, are kept together on today's feast.
screen: `A GUEST, A BUSY KITCHEN.` → `ONE SISTER LISTENING.` → `TELL HER TO HELP ME.`

segments.voice: Luke tells the kitchen scene. Martha welcomes Jesus into her house. Mary sits at his feet. Martha, busy with much serving, asks him to send her sister to help. Jesus answers her gently, saying her name twice. In the Douay-Rheims: "Martha, Martha, thou art careful, and art troubled about many things." Careful here means full of cares. He goes on: one thing is necessary, and Mary has chosen the best part. It's easy to hear that as a scolding, and some readers stop there and side with Martha. But look where the story starts: Martha is the one who opened the door. Without her there's no house, no meal, no place for Mary to sit. Now John's Gospel. Lazarus, their brother, falls sick, and the sisters send word to Jesus. By the time he comes, Lazarus has been in the tomb for days. And who goes out down the road to meet him? Martha. She tells him straight that if he'd been there, her brother wouldn't have died. A few lines later, she says she believes he is the Christ, the Son of God. At the tomb, John writes, "Jesus wept." Then he calls Lazarus out. So the house at Bethany holds three ways of loving the same friend: Martha's work and her bold faith, Mary's listening, and Lazarus, who simply comes back to the table. The Church keeps all three on one day now. Not the busy one against the quiet one. A household.
screen: `MARTHA, MARTHA.` · `SHE OPENED THE DOOR.` · `SHE GOES OUT TO MEET HIM.` · `THREE WAYS OF LOVING ONE FRIEND.` · then, large: `JESUS WEPT.`

segments.voice: Think of someone you could welcome, a friend, a neighbor, someone new in town, and picture them at your table. Notice the Martha in you, already planning the cooking and the cleaning; let that go for a moment and be Mary, just glad they're there, listening. If you pray, ask God to bless that table; if you don't, simply hold the person in mind.
Martha. The sister of Mary and Lazarus in Bethany, who welcomed Jesus into her house, worried over the serving, and went out to meet him with bold faith.
Your line: the house at bethany. The work and the listening both belong at that table. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the memorial of Saints Martha, Mary and Lazarus on 29 July, hearing Martha's story from the Gospels of Luke or John at Mass.

fork.setup: you're Martha. your brother has died, and Jesus has finally arrived, days late. what do you do?
options: stay home and refuse to see him.
go out to meet him on the road.

fork.reveal: Martha went out to meet him, told him straight her brother needn't have died, then said she believed he is the Christ.

chat.says: Wasn't Martha the one Jesus scolded for doing too much?
options: He spoke gently, but she also opened her home and said he was the Christ.
Yes. Jesus told her to stop serving and never cook for guests again.
No. Jesus praised Martha for working while Mary sat doing nothing.
chat.meaning: Jesus said Martha, Martha gently. She opened the door to him, and in John she goes out to meet him and says she believes he is the Christ.
